# linux_mount (Resource)

Mounts a file system, and records it in `/etc/fstab` so that it is mounted at boot, like Ansible's `mount` module. Also enables swap areas (`fstype = "swap"`).

An existing fstab entry for the same mount point (or swap device) is replaced. When the file system was already mounted, or listed in fstab, before the resource was created, destroying the resource leaves it as it is; otherwise it is unmounted and removed from fstab. Mount points are created when needed and never removed.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Mount a data disk at boot, by UUID: device names may change.
resource "linux_mount" "data" {
  path    = "/data"
  device  = "UUID=${linux_filesystem.data.uuid}"
  fstype  = "ext4"
  options = "defaults,noatime,nofail"
  pass    = 2
}

# An NFS share.
resource "linux_mount" "shared" {
  path    = "/mnt/shared"
  device  = "nfs.example.com:/exports/shared"
  fstype  = "nfs"
  options = "defaults,_netdev"
}

# A swap area.
resource "linux_mount" "swap" {
  device = "UUID=${linux_filesystem.swap.uuid}"
  fstype = "swap"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `device` (String) What to mount: `UUID=<uuid>` (recommended, see `linux_filesystem.uuid`), `LABEL=<label>`, a device path, `server:/export` for NFS, `tmpfs`...
- `fstype` (String) File system type, such as `ext4`, `xfs`, `nfs`, `tmpfs` or `swap`.

### Optional

- `dump` (Number) Fifth fstab field, used by `dump`. Defaults to `0`.
- `fstab` (String) File system table to edit. systemd is reloaded after `/etc/fstab` changes. Defaults to `/etc/fstab`.
- `mounted` (Boolean) Mount the file system now. With `false`, it is unmounted if mounted, and only recorded in fstab. Defaults to `true`.
- `options` (String) Mount options, comma-separated, such as `defaults,noatime,nofail`. Changing them remounts the file system. Defaults to `defaults`.
- `pass` (Number) Sixth fstab field: order of the file system checks at boot, `1` for the root file system, `2` for others, `0` for none. Defaults to `0`.
- `path` (String) Mount point, such as `/data`. Required, except for swap areas.
- `persist` (Boolean) Record the mount in `fstab`, so that it is mounted at boot. Defaults to `true`.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Mount point, or device for swap areas.
